references.text: Jacob gives instructions about his burial in the cave of Machpelah, expressing the same wish as in 47:30 to be buried with his ancestors.
Abraham was buried in the cave of Machpelah by Isaac and Ishmael—the very grave site Jacob wished to be laid in.
Abraham purchased the cave of Machpelah as a burial place, which became the family's burial ground and the place where Jacob desired to rest.
Jacob's sons fulfill his wish by burying him in the cave of Machpelah, where Abraham and Isaac are buried.
Joseph gives similar instructions that his bones should be taken out of Egypt, showing that the promise of the land was important to the patriarchs.

The book of Hebrews mentions Joseph's instructions regarding his bones as an expression of faith, confirming the biblical pattern in which the patriarchs linked their burial to God's promise of the land.
Contrast between delaying God's call for burials (Luke) and completing burials as a holy duty before returning home (Genesis).
Direct retelling of the same oath and instruction from Jacob to Joseph in two consecutive chapters.
Direct fulfillment of the oaths from 47:30; Pharaoh recognizes and permits burial in Canaan.
Direct precursor: Jacob gives the instructions in 49:29, which are confirmed and sworn to in 47:30.
